docker-compose-generator.assumptionNote: Values containing colons, spaces, or special characters are automatically quoted so the YAML stays valid.
benefits: No YAML syntax to memorize — fill in forms and get a valid docker-compose.yml.
Add unlimited services; each becomes its own top-level service block.
Ports, environment variables, and volumes are parsed from simple comma or line lists.
Restart policies use the official Docker values with plain-language labels.
Download the file directly or copy it — ready for docker compose up.

faqs.a: Fill in at least a service name and image, then copy the YAML or download docker-compose.yml. Place the file in your project folder and run docker compose up -d.
faqs.q: How do I use the generated file?

faqs.a: Type ports as host:container pairs separated by commas, for example 8080:80, 443:443. Each pair becomes one quoted entry under ports.
faqs.q: How do I write the ports field?

faqs.a: Put one KEY=value pair per line, for example NODE_ENV=production on the first line and PORT=3000 on the second. Each line becomes one list entry under environment.
faqs.q: How do I write environment variables?

faqs.a: One per line in host-path:container-path form, for example ./data:/data or pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data. Named volumes like pgdata need a top-level volumes block, which you add manually.
unless-stopped restarts the container always, except when you stop it yourself. always restarts even after a manual stop. on-failure restarts only after a crash. no never restarts.
faqs.q: Which restart policy should I choose?

faqs.a: This generator covers the common subset: image, ports, environment, volumes, and restart. For networks, depends_on, healthchecks, or build sections, add them to the YAML manually after generating.
faqs.q: Can it generate networks and depends_on?

docker-compose-generator.formula:
ports:        "HOST:CONTAINER" per comma-separated entry
environment: "KEY=VALUE" per line
volumes:      "HOST:CONTAINER" per line
restart:      no | always | unless-stopped | on-failure
howTo: Click Add service for each container your app needs.
Enter the service name and Docker image, for example nginx:1.25.
Add ports as comma-separated host:container pairs.
Add environment variables and volumes, one per line.
Choose a restart policy, then copy or download the YAML.
keyFacts: docker-compose.yml declares multi-container apps in a single YAML file.
Each service needs an image; ports map host ports to container ports.
Environment entries use the KEY=value list format under each service.
Restart policies control what Docker does when a container stops or the host reboots.
Values with colons or spaces are auto-quoted so the YAML parses correctly.
docker-compose-generator.keywords: docker compose generator, docker-compose.yml builder, compose file generator, docker yaml generator
limitations: Only the common subset is generated: image, ports, environment, volumes, restart.
Named volumes need a top-level volumes block that you add manually.
Networks, depends_on, healthchecks, and build sections are not generated.
Service names are slugified; exotic characters are replaced with dashes.

docker-compose-generator.quickAnswer: A docker-compose.yml file describes all the containers an app needs — web server, database, cache — so one docker compose up command starts everything. This tool builds that YAML from simple forms: add services, type images, ports, environment variables and volumes, and download a valid compose file.
docker-compose-generator.tagline: Build a valid docker-compose.yml from simple forms — no YAML memorization.
docker-compose-generator.workedExample:
One service named web with image nginx:1.25, ports 8080:80, environment NODE_ENV=production, restart unless-stopped.

Generated docker-compose.yml:
services:
  web:
    image: "nginx:1.25"
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    environment:
      - "NODE_ENV=production"
    restart: unless-stopped

Save as docker-compose.yml and run docker compose up -d to start nginx on http://localhost:8080.
